chapter.title: What an agent is, and what it is not

cards.body: Picture a small desk by the window. Every morning at 7, someone sits down with the same 5 newspapers, a pair of scissors, and a notepad. By 7:20 there is one note on your desk: 3 lines about your rivals, each clipping pinned next to it. **An agent is that person, done as a program.** It wakes on its own, reads the same places, and leaves you a note.
cards.simpler: Imagine a small desk by a window. Every morning at 7, someone sits down with the same 5 newspapers, a pair of scissors and a notepad. By 7:20 there is one note on your desk: 3 short lines about your rivals, with each clipping pinned beside it. **An agent is that person, turned into a program.** It wakes up on its own, reads the same places every day, and leaves you a note.

cards.prompt: Your clipping person turns up every morning, reads the 5 papers, cuts out rival stories, writes the note. Which of these is NOT part of their job?

options.text: Showing up at 7 without being called
Deciding on their own to also start reading 20 new magazines
Writing a short note and pinning the clippings to it

whyNot.a: That's the trigger, the alarm clock: the agent starts on a schedule without you. It is very much part of the job.
whyNot.c: That's the output, the note on your desk. Without it you'd have to read the papers yourself.

cards.reteach: The clipping person does a fixed, repeating job: wake up, read agreed sources, write a note. They do not wander off and invent new tasks. An agent is the same. It runs a set routine on its own. It does not decide its own goals.

cards.title: A program that runs by itself
cards.body:
An *agent* here means a small program that runs without you pressing a button each time. It starts on a schedule, does a fixed list of steps, and stops. **The key word is unattended.** You are asleep, and it still works.

The steps are ordinary. Download a web page. Compare it with yesterday's copy. Send a message. Most of an agent is plain plumbing that any script could do.

The one special step is the reader. The agent hands text to an *AI model*, a program that reads and writes language, and asks it to explain what changed in plain words. That step is what makes the note readable instead of a wall of raw text.
cards.simpler: An agent is a small program that runs without you pressing a button. It starts on a schedule, does its steps, and stops. **The key word is unattended.** It works while you sleep. Most steps are plain. Download a page. Compare it with yesterday's copy. Send a message. The one special step is the reader. The agent hands text to an AI model, a program that reads and writes language, and asks it to say what changed in plain words.

cards.title: Tuesday, 7:03am
cards.body: Maya runs a small invoicing tool. On Tuesday at 7:03am her agent woke, fetched 4 competitor pricing pages, and found that 3 had not changed at all. One had. The note on her phone said: "Rival B's Pro plan went from $29 to $35 a month. Source: pricing page, line 'Pro – $35/mo'." Maya read it in 10 seconds over coffee. The agent had done 4 downloads, 4 comparisons and 1 model call, and she saw none of it.
cards.simpler: Maya runs a small invoicing tool. On Tuesday at 7:03am her agent woke up, fetched 4 competitor pricing pages, and found that 3 had not changed at all. One had. The note on her phone said: "Rival B's Pro plan went from $29 to $35 a month. Source: pricing page, line 'Pro – $35/mo'." Maya read it in 10 seconds over coffee. Behind the scenes the agent did 4 downloads, 4 comparisons and 1 model call. **She saw none of it.**

cards.prompt: Maya's note said "Rival B's Pro plan went from $29 to $35." Which part of the agent wrote that sentence?

options.text: The trigger, because it ran at 7:03
The model, because it turned the changed line into plain English
The source, because the pricing page contained the new price

whyNot.a: That's the alarm clock. It only decides when to start, it never writes a word.
whyNot.c: That's the newspaper. The page had the raw line 'Pro – $35/mo', but someone had to read it and say what it means.

cards.reteach: Four parts: the trigger starts things, sources hold the raw pages, the model reads and explains, the output delivers the note. Only one of those produces sentences. The model is the reader with the pen.

cards.title: The 4 boxes
cards.body:
Every competitor-tracking agent has the same 4 parts. Draw them as 4 boxes left to right.

Box 1 is the **trigger**: the alarm clock. A schedule that says "run at 7am daily". Box 2 is the **sources**: the newspapers. A short list of exact web addresses. Box 3 is the model: the reader. It gets the changed text and writes 2 plain sentences. Box 4 is the output: the note on your desk. An email, a chat message, a file.

The model is 1 box out of 4. People hear "AI agent" and imagine the model is everything. Here it is one worker in a small office of plumbing.
cards.simpler: Every competitor-tracking agent has the same 4 parts. Box 1 is the **trigger**, the alarm clock: a schedule that says run at 7am daily. Box 2 is the sources, the newspapers: a short list of exact web addresses. Box 3 is the model, the reader: it writes 2 plain sentences. Box 4 is the output, the note on your desk: an email, chat message or file. The model is only 1 box out of 4. The rest is plain plumbing.

cards.body: Dev heard "agent" and opened a chat window, pasted 5 competitor addresses, and typed "watch these for me". The chat replied warmly and then forgot everything when he closed the tab. He had a reader with no alarm clock, no saved newspapers and no note. You spot this mistake when the "agent" only works while you are typing to it. **If it needs you awake, it is not yet an agent.**
cards.simpler: Dev heard the word "agent" and opened a chat window. He pasted 5 competitor web addresses and typed "watch these for me". The chat answered warmly, then forgot everything when he closed the tab. He had a reader, but no alarm clock, no saved newspapers and no note. You can spot this mistake easily: the "agent" only works while you are typing to it. **If it needs you awake, it is not yet an agent.**

cards.prompt: A friend says: "I built a competitor agent! I ask the AI every morning what changed on their sites." What is missing from the 4 boxes?

options.text: The model, because asking an AI is not the same as using a model
The trigger, because your friend is the alarm clock, not the program
Nothing, that is a complete agent

whyNot.a: That's the one box they do have: the AI they ask is the reader. The gap is elsewhere.
whyNot.c: That's the chat-window trap from the mistake card: if it needs a person to start it each day, the trigger box is empty.

cards.reteach: Ask one question of any so-called agent: who starts it? If a person has to type something each morning, the trigger is a human, not a schedule. An agent needs its own alarm clock.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: An agent is a program that wakes on a schedule, reads a fixed set of pages, asks an AI model to say what changed, and drops a short note where you will see it. **It is 4 boxes: trigger, sources, model, output.** Only the third one is AI.
cards.simpler: An agent is a program that wakes up on a schedule, reads a fixed set of pages, asks an AI model to say what changed, and drops a short note where you will see it. **It is 4 boxes: trigger, sources, model, output.** Only the third box is AI. Everything else is ordinary plumbing.

cards.body: Take any scrap of paper. Draw 4 boxes in a row and label them trigger, sources, model, output. Under each, write one real thing: 7am, your top rival's pricing page, "explain in 2 sentences", your email. Keep it for chapter 2.
cards.simpler: Take any scrap of paper. **Draw 4 boxes in a row** and label them trigger, sources, model, output. Under each box, write one real thing from your own life: 7am, your top rival's pricing page, "explain in 2 sentences", your email address. Keep it for chapter 2.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now draw the 4 boxes of a competitor-tracking agent on paper and say what each one does.
